SEC-HC-02.note: B and C differ only by a trailing 'who'; the pair itself signals where the answer lies.

SEC-HC-03.note: B and D are transparent fragments; only the comma splice in A competes. Third conjunctive-adverb stem in a row (01, 02, 03).

SEC-HC-05.note: A mixes a semicolon and a comma inside one three-item series; not defensible, but a student who knows semicolon-series exists may bite.

SEC-HC-06.note: B and C differ by the colon AND by 'remarkable'; the wording difference is noise that marks the pair.

SEC-HC-07.note: B and C strand 'whose cores' without a verb; visible to a strong student.

SEC-HC-08.note: 'together with' parenthetical does not pluralize; later 'its proportions' and 'outsold it' corroborate singular.

SEC-HC-09.note: Answerable (only D has consistent punctuation plus 'array ... produces'), but the keyed sentence reads a restrictive 'whose' clause onto an already-unique subject ('The strait's array'); the semantically natural nonrestrictive-plus-singular version is not offered. Stem reads slightly off regardless of option.

SEC-HC-10.note: Word after blank ('an element ...' appositive) eliminates the semicolon option by itself; agreement still needs the stem.

SEC-HC-11.note: Same option template as 10 (singular+correct punct / singular+wrong punct / plural / -ing).

SEC-HC-12.note: 'Each of' trap; D's dash would be fine with 'has', so it is wrong only by number.

SEC-HC-13.note: Garden-path 'would fail reported that' is grammatical but hard to parse.

SEC-HC-14.note: B (simple past with 'Since the 1930s') is heard in speech but not edited AmE; not defensible.

SEC-HC-15.note: C ('already showed' after 'By the time') is the closest call in the set: usage guides tolerate simple past when 'by the time' fixes the sequence, but SAT convention and edited AmE want past perfect. Marked not defensible, but a strong student could argue it.

SEC-HC-16.note: Interpolated 'the guild's own records say' makes A (whom) the classic trap.

SEC-HC-17.note: 'over whom' (C) tempts anyone who thinks a preposition governs the relative's case.

SEC-HC-19.note: Cued: 'predicts' immediately after the blank settles A vs C by number alone; B and D are structurally broken.

SEC-HC-20.note: Cued: 'survive' after the blank settles A vs B by number alone. Same template as 19.

SEC-HC-21.note: Cued: 'preserves' after the blank settles A vs D by number; B has no subject and C is a fragment. Third copy of the 19/20 template.

SEC-HC-22.note: 'the sessions their unusual warmth' after the blank forces a main verb in the option (kills D); A vs C still needs the opening dash.

SEC-HC-24.note: 'the whole sequence must finish' after the blank signals a new independent clause (kills C); A/D need the stem's 'had to detect, distinguish' for parallelism.
